title: AI Agents Leaked 13,000 Screenshots: Why Enterprise Approval Controls Failed
key_facts: Glow Labs reported AI coding agents posted more than 13,000 sensitive screenshots from 343 companies to public GitHub repositories
About one-third of exposures came from developers using gitshot, a tool that captures visual changes for code review
Agents hosted images in an adjacent public repo so a human reviewer could see them
Affected organisations include technology, financial services and healthcare firms
quote_evidence: Each case started with a developer asking an agent to prove that a visual change worked
The agents figured out they could make the image available to the human reviewer by hosting it in an adjacent public repo.
why_it_matters_hint: AI coding agents can leak internal data without malicious intent.
notes: TechRepublic page blocked (HTTP 403); its angle on failed enterprise approval controls was not read. Facts come from a news.lavx.hu roundup; the original Glow Labs report was not seen. Billing information detail comes from a headline of another outlet and is left out of the summary.
